data.mechanism: _phrases only emits 4-word windows with trailing punctuation

chunk_findings.detail: The stripped variant is inserted into the phrase set without re-checking it against the length floor, so the `_SHORT_MIN`/`_PHRASE_MIN` guard the surrounding code (and the new test `test_three_short_words_are_not_a_phrase`) relies on is bypassed for any fragment quoted at both ends. Concretely, for the source line `raise X("value is wrong")` the 3-word window `"value is wrong`…`wrong"` is 16 chars and passes `len(phrase) >= _SHORT_MIN`, and then `phrase.strip(_EDGE)` adds the 14-character phrase `value is wrong`, which is below the documented minimum of 15 that exists precisely so ordinary short English is not treated as a phrase. The same happens for 4-word windows (floor 16): `'"abc def ghi jk"'` yields the 14-char phrase `abc def ghi jk`. Those sub-floor entries are generic enough to match unrelated tests through `phrase_tests`, i.e. the change trades the recall it was meant to fix for over-selection that the guard was designed to prevent; the guard should be applied to the stripped string (or the stripped result checked against the same floor) before adding it.

chunk_findings.detail:
`out.add(phrase.strip(_EDGE))` runs unconditionally inside `if len(phrase) >= floor`, so the *stripped* string is committed to the phrase set without its own length (or emptiness) check. `_EDGE` contains only space/punctuation (`" ,.;:()[]`'\""`), so any window whose words are themselves punchuation-only tokens strips to `""`.

Concretely, a message such as `split on ',', ';', ':'` yields the 3-word window `',', ';', ':'` (15 chars, so `len(phrase) >= _SHORT_MIN` passes); `phrase.strip(_EDGE)` is `""`, which is then added to the returned set. Any consumer that tests containment (`phrase in test_source`, or a regex built from the phrase) matches `""` against every test, so the selection degenerates to "all tests" for that change. A milder instance of the same bug is any phrase whose strip drops it below the floor — e.g. `_phrases(['"uses the flags,"'])` adds `uses the flags` (14 chars), even though `_SHORT_MIN = 15` is documented as the cutoff. The change's own guard test does not catch this: its input `'"it is a of the"'` has no window reaching 15/16 chars at all, so the `len(p) < 15` assertion never exercises the strip path.
